headline: Crucial Blackwell packaging steps remain offshore despite US chip supply chain growth by Nvidia & Intel
summary: Nvidia and Intel highlight growing US chip manufacturing, with Blackwell wafers now produced in Arizona. However, advanced packaging for these chips and all HBM production still occur overseas, with US facilities not expected until 2028.
details: Nvidia proudly announced its US manufacturing network spans 43 states, with TSMC's Phoenix plant producing Blackwell wafers at volume. The company plans to produce up to $500 billion of AI infrastructure in the U.S. over four years with partners including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, Corning, Coherent, and Amkor.

Intel also presented its end-to-end U.S. capabilities across design, manufacturing, and advanced packaging. Both companies' claims hold true for wafer production, but omit a critical downstream step: advanced packaging.

Every Blackwell die from TSMC's Arizona fab still travels across the Pacific to Taiwan for CoWoS-L packaging. This means a Blackwell die fabbed in Arizona travels approximately 7,000 miles to be diced, stacked, and mounted before returning to the U.S.

Furthermore, no HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) is currently manufactured or packaged on U.S. soil. All HBM production comes from SK hynix, Samsung, or Micron facilities in South Korea, Taiwan, and Japan.

Despite these gaps, leading-edge logic wafers are now being fabricated in the U.S. by two companies on two competing nodes: TSMC's 4NP for Nvidia's Blackwell and Intel's 18A. This represents a significant achievement compared to the start of the decade.

Future efforts aim to close these gaps. Foxconn is building a Houston factory for GB300 tray modules, and Wistron will assemble Nvidia AI systems in Fort Worth. Amkor also broke ground on a $7 billion packaging campus in Arizona, though these facilities won't start production until 2028 at the earliest. Intel's Foveros operation in New Mexico currently handles its own 3D-stacked products and is attracting outside interest, with Google reportedly booking Intel to package over 3 million TPUs in 2028.

headline_marked: [[Sky (Comcast) acquires ITV]] for £2.1B, becoming UK's second largest broadcaster
headline: Sky (Comcast) acquires ITV for £2.1B, becoming UK's second largest broadcaster
summary: Sky, owned by Comcast, is paying £2.1 billion ($2.8 billion) for ITV's media and entertainment business, including its broadcast channels and ITVX platform. This move aims to compete with global streaming giants.
details: Sky, a Comcast-owned company, has confirmed its acquisition of ITV's media and entertainment business for £2.1 billion (approximately $2.8 billion). This deal includes ITV's free-to-air broadcast channels and its on-demand platform, ITVX.

If approved by regulators, this acquisition would make Sky the UK's second-biggest broadcaster, trailing only the BBC. Sky stated that "scale matters more than ever" to compete with global streaming services and YouTube.

The deal faces scrutiny from regulators already concerned about market plurality following other major media mergers. ITV will retain its Studios business, responsible for shows like "The Voice" and "Love Island."
As part of the agreement, Sky will take control of Love Productions, the company behind popular series such as "The Great British Baking Show" and "The Great British Sewing Bee."
